solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Something worth having when fixed

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as the sun rose'
set means fixed or firmly established

explanation.surface: Something valuable becomes even more so once it is fixed in place, like a fixed capital item on a balance sheet.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the accounting term 'fixed asset', but 'when fixed' is the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A resource or quality that is useful or valuable is a thing worth having.

clue.text: 10 parts noble, Henry drops in 11

indicators.note: drops in means the king's initial falls from the front and lands inside the number
parts means splits apart, so the number gets into the middle of the noble word

parts.note: handsome can mean noble or generous, as in 'a handsome gesture'
the number in the clue is read as the word ten, not as a reference to another light
H is the abbreviation for henry, the unit of inductance, and the initial of a king's name

explanation.surface: A cross-reference clue: the number splits a word for noble, and Henry slips into it.
explanation.walkthrough: The 10 is not a cross-reference to 10 across: it is just the number ten. 'drops in' moves Henry's initial from the front of the noble word into the number.
explanation.definitionFit: The solution of 11 means 'and more so', which is exactly what this phrase means too.

clue.text: Get excited about aircraft's first flight

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for get excited goes round the letter

parts.note: to stir is to rouse or get worked up

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of aircraft's

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled about the first flight of a new plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' looks like air travel to match the aircraft, but it is a set of steps.
explanation.definitionFit: In older and Scottish usage a stair is a whole series of steps, which is a flight.

clue.text: Rock not completely protecting tit or chat

indicators.note: protecting means shielding, so the shortened word surrounds the word for tit
not completely means the last letter of the word for rock is cut off

parts.note: to teeter is to rock unsteadily
a tit is a teat or nipple

explanation.surface: A rock almost sheltering a little bird or a chat, another small songbird.
explanation.walkthrough: Tit and chat are both small birds, so the surface reads like birdwatching. 'not completely' trims TEETER to TEETE.
explanation.definitionFit: A private conversation between two people is called by this French phrase meaning head to head.

clue.text: Arty types cry about arresting one nicking bit of beefcake

indicators.note: arresting means holding, so the reversed cry holds the rest inside it
about tells us the word for cry turns round

parts.note: to sob is to cry

indicators.note: nicking means slipping in to steal, so the one gets into the muscleman

parts.note: a he-man is a muscular hunk, a bit of beefcake
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Arty people moan about one of their number pinching a hunky man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit of beefcake' looks like a chunk of meat, but it is a he-man, a muscular hunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Unconventional artists and writers living free lives are called bohemians, after the Romani supposedly from Bohemia.

clue.text: I see Tessa is at the drawing board again!

parts.note: read as wordplay, the phrase says take the 1 across light, which starts in square one, and read it backwards towards that square: the letters give the name Tessa

explanation.surface: Someone spots Tessa back at her drawing board, starting the design over.
explanation.walkthrough: This depends on the grid: 1 across starts at square one, and reading its letters back towards that square spells TESSA.
explanation.definitionFit: Going back to the drawing board means starting again from scratch, the meaning of the idiom.

clue.text: Perhaps Mexican meal vouchers are being distributed with nosh?

indicators.note: being distributed means being spread around, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Meal tickets handed out along with food, maybe at a Mexican restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: Ranch-style eggs, a typical Mexican breakfast dish of fried eggs on tortillas with salsa.

clue.text: Mess up a quantity of goods imported from the east

indicators.note: from the east says the hidden letters are read backwards
a quantity of means only some of the letters of goods imported are taken

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Bungling a shipment of goods brought in from Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'a quantity' into the definition; 'a quantity of' marks the hidden letters, leaving 'Mess up' as the definition. In an across-the-page reading 'from the east' means right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: To bungle or do something wrongly is to make a mess of it.

clue.text: One's had one's fill, poor punk

parts.note: a means one, as in 'a pound' for one pound

indicators.note: punk means rotten or worthless, so the letters are in a bad state and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone has eaten their fill, a scruffy punk rocker perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's had' means someone has been tricked: the person fooled by a prank on 1 April.
explanation.definitionFit: The victim of a 1 April prank has been 'had', meaning hoaxed or taken in.

clue.text: Notes help me!

definitions.meaning: so (or soh) is a note of the sol-fa scale, and these are two of them
a distress call sent by ships in trouble

explanation.surface: Someone scribbling notes asking for assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of the scale note so, and the Morse distress signal crying for rescue.

clue.text: Are they called for to resolve issue with Mastercard?

indicators.note: to resolve is to break down into parts, so the letters are separated and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A cardholder asks whether a problem with a credit card needs extreme action to sort it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a question: when a problem looks hopeless, severe steps are what is called for.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme steps taken in a crisis are the kind of action people say 'is called for' when nothing milder will do.

clue.text: The way bumbling fat local trod boards presumably not this!

indicators.note: boards means takes on board, so the word for the way holds the jumbled letters

parts.note: how means the way, as in 'that's how it's done'

indicators.note: bumbling means clumsy and muddled, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A clumsy, overweight local who treads the boards in amateur dramatics is hardly a performer others dread succeeding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boards' looks like part of 'trod the boards' (acted on stage) but signals containment. The definition is ironic: after the bumbling actor, the next act need not fear comparison.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer so good that whoever comes next suffers by comparison; the clumsy local actor is the opposite.

clue.text: 1 down handles attached

definitions.meaning: the phrase at 1 down means 'and more so', a matching idiom
taken literally, door knobs fixed onto something

explanation.surface: A cross-reference to another light, plus doors with their handles fitted.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom, chiefly British, means 'and even more so', as in 'the same to you, with bells on'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means 'and more besides', the same as 1 down; literally, it is fitted with door handles.

clue.text: Breathing easier, it seems, after using handkerchief and tie?

indicators.note: once a handkerchief has cleared it, the breathing organ has an opening put inside it

parts.note: the nose is the organ one breathes through
O, an open ring, pictures the clear passage that makes breathing easier

explanation.surface: Someone with a cold blows their nose and feels relief, then ties a knot.
explanation.walkthrough: A whimsical clue: blowing your nose opens it up, so an O (a round opening) goes inside NOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose is a loop tied in rope with a running knot, so it is a kind of tie.

clue.text: Presumably not so well in shop?

parts.note: out can mean not in, as in a fashion that is out, the opposite of the word in that follows
fitter means more well, healthier

explanation.surface: Someone apparently feeling less healthy while in a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Presumably' warns that the clue is read loosely: 'not ... in' gives OUT and 'so well' gives FITTER, the reverse of what 'not so well' seems to say.
explanation.definitionFit: A clothing retailer, especially one selling outdoor gear, is a kind of shop.

clue.text: Dismiss repeated calls for action

definitions.meaning: to dismiss a batter in baseball, or delete words, is to cross them off
a union leader's two cries 'Strike!' and 'Out!' both urge workers to walk off the job

explanation.surface: A boss sacks someone after repeated demands that something be done.
explanation.definitionFit: In baseball a pitcher dismisses a batter with three strikes; and two cries rallying a workforce to industrial action.

clue.text: Novel reason for Billy's capture?

definitions.meaning: a Robert Louis Stevenson adventure story about David Balfour
the outlaw Billy the Kid caught while asleep: the young goat dozed

explanation.surface: Asking what book explains how someone called Billy was caught.
explanation.walkthrough: Billy the Kid was an American outlaw; a billy is also a male goat, whose young is a kid.
explanation.definitionFit: Stevenson's 1886 adventure novel, and literally the outlaw having nodded off when caught.

clue.text: Going off at Maggotts or Stowe?

definitions.meaning: milk going sour is said to be going off
Maggotts and Stowe are bends on the Silverstone motor-racing circuit, so a car there is cornering

explanation.surface: A racing driver going off the track at one of the circuit's famous corners.
explanation.walkthrough: Silverstone is the home of the British Grand Prix; Maggotts and Stowe are two of its corners, and 'Maggotts' also hints at food going bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Food or milk beginning to sour is said to be going off, and a car rounding a bend is cornering.

clue.text: It exterminates product of yeast that's in decay, reportedly

indicators.note: that's in means the beer is placed inside the letters for the sound
reportedly means as heard, so the word decay is spoken and written as the letters it sounds like

parts.note: the word decay, said aloud, sounds like the two letters D and K
ale is brewed by yeast fermentation

explanation.surface: Something wipes out a yeast product that has gone off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' turns 'decay' into the letters D K, said aloud; ALE goes between them.
explanation.definitionFit: The robotic villains of Doctor Who are famous for their cry of 'Exterminate!'

clue.text: The military show what was done in Holyrood parlour?

definitions.meaning: a tattoo is a display of military music and marching held each summer at Edinburgh Castle

definitions.text: what was done in Holyrood parlour?
definitions.meaning: Holyrood is a district of the Scottish capital, so a design inked in a parlour there is a Scottish-capital skin decoration

explanation.surface: A display of soldiers, and a design inked in a parlour in Holyrood.
explanation.walkthrough: Holyrood is the area of Edinburgh home to the royal palace and the Scottish Parliament; a tattoo parlour inks designs on skin.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous annual military pageant at Edinburgh Castle, and literally an inked design made in that city.

clue.text: Copper coin of old times

parts.note: a bob was the old British shilling
by means times in multiplication, as in 'three by four'

explanation.surface: A penny-type coin from long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like the metal of an old coin, but it is slang for a police officer; a bobby is a British policeman, after Sir Robert Peel.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal British words for a police officer.

clue.text: A jolly lot put together a little house-warming?

indicators.note: put together means joined up, so the words for the group run on as one word

parts.note: a lot as a whole body is 'the' group, so the definite article heads the phrase
a jolly is slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM

explanation.surface: A cheerful crowd gathering to warm a new home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A jolly lot' is THE RM, the Royal Marines as a body; 'put together' closes the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of heat used in gas billing is a small amount of warmth for a home.

clue.text: We lay down our lives for others

definitions.text: We lay down our lives for others

parts.words: We lay down our lives for others
parts.note: sounds like heroic self-sacrifice, but laying down a life here means writing it down for readers

explanation.surface: Soldiers or martyrs declaring that they sacrifice themselves for the sake of others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay down our lives' is an idiom for dying for a cause; here it means setting down one's own life story on paper for others to read.
explanation.definitionFit: Writers of their own life stories record their lives for the benefit of readers.

clue.text: Once-yearly gathering of swagmen

indicators.note: of means taken out of, so the letters lie inside the word

explanation.surface: An annual meeting of Australian itinerant workers.
explanation.walkthrough: Swagmen were Australian itinerant workers who carried their belongings in a swag.
explanation.definitionFit: The annual general meeting of a company or club happens once each year.

clue.text: Exercise early with some swimmers

indicators.note: to exercise is to work something about, so these letters are put through their paces into a new order

explanation.surface: Getting up early to work out alongside some fellow swimmers.
explanation.definitionFit: These are snake-like fish of tropical reefs, so they are creatures that swim.

clue.text: I show spirit how to work in office

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation for a way of working goes inside the word for office

parts.note: a den is a private study or office
MO is modus operandi, a way of working

explanation.surface: Someone boasting of their energy as they show a newcomer how to get things done at work.
explanation.definitionFit: An evil spirit or fiend of folklore is a demon.
